key_terms.الإِقْرَار: Acknowledgment or confession of a fact
key_terms.البَيَانَة: Proof or evidence (specifically of birth or lineage)
key_terms.الحَمِيل: Captives or displaced persons who claim kinship without formal documentation
key_terms.الشِّرْك: Polytheism (used here to denote the pre-Islamic or general period of captivity before Islam)
key_terms.الصِّحَّة: Soundness/health (referring to the mental and physical state of the claimants)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance for captives claiming kinship without formal proof?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiquing the prevailing juristic view that denied inheritance to captives lacking formal proof of kinship, arguing instead that continuous, mutual acknowledgment (*iqrar*) in a state of sanity suffices. This highlights the Shia emphasis on practical social reality and presumptive continuity (*istishab*) over rigid evidentiary formalism in matters of family law.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Muhammed bin Hussain, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdul-Rahman bin Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

I asked him about the hameel, and he said: And what thing is hameel? I said: A woman who is taken as captive from her land and with her is a small child, and so she says: «He is my son», and a man who is taken as captive and meets his brother, and so he says: «He is my brother», while they have no proof except for their saying. He said: And what do the people among you say? I said: That they do not pass on inheritance to them if they have no proof of their birth; that the birth was only in a period of polytheism. He said: Glory be to Allah (how strange that is). If she brings her son or daughter, and she does not cease from declare it, and if the man recognizes his brother and it would be by the declaration of both as correct, and they do not cease to declare that, they will inherit each other.
